articleTitle: Optimize SRM Rotor Geometry Analysis for 3kW Light Electric Vehicle Grade Performances
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: To promote a sustainable future using Electric Vehicles (EVs) mostly depends on low-cost Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM). The Mechanical characteristics of SRM perfectly suit EV drive operating conditions as compared to other rotational electrical machines. SRM is an excellent choice for an EVs drive due to its benefits such as simple design, high fault switching capability, wide operating frequency, constant power at high-speed range, high temperature, and high efficiency. The proposed work involves designing an EV-grade 300kg drive with the finest duty cycle characteristics. The 8/6 geometry was used to optimize the 3 kW, 3000 rpm SRM architecture. The finite element approach is used to examine the design of rotor shape and teeth topology modifications in the round, straight, taper and round, taper and straight, and straight and round. It is described the modified SRM double pole compares in terms of efficiency, line current, rated torque and power. To evaluate the effectiveness of SRM-EVs at low-speed 500rpm, the enhanced geometry model assessments were performed by JMAG software and compared with various rotor geometry adjustments.

articleTitle: Modeling and Attenuation of Conducted EMI in DC-DC Converters Using Hybrid Filter
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) in automobiles is regulated by extensive standards due to its criticality of operation. One of the major equipment contributing to the EMI emissions is the usage of power converters for various applications across the automobile. Predominantly, the power converters used in automobiles to drive all the electronic components are DC-DC converters in order to meet the voltage requirements of these individual equipment driven by a fixed voltage output battery. The ask of the modern age is to have high-power density converters in order to have compactness in the overall equipment. This high-power density is possible with the usage of wide band gap devices as the switches in the converter circuits which enable high switching frequency operation. The flip side is, however, the EMI emissions due to these high-frequency switching devices. EMI modeling and reduction research is the key to developing solutions to achieve EMI compliance. The work focuses on the typically used buck-boost converter with practical application. Addressing all types of EMI emissions involve different strategy and modeling specific to the type of EMI emission. The entire design and development flow of the converter complying with the standards of EMI is laid out in the work that follows.

articleTitle: Design and IoT Implementation of a Long Range laser Based Intrusion Detection System for Perimeter Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Traditional perimeter surveillance systems addressing territorial security concerns typically comprise checkpoints, patrolling and human-involved strategies. Since such systems involve human errors, electronic surveillance solutions have gained significant importance. However, long range perimeter surveillance systems have not been reported in literature. This paper presents the architecture of an Internet of Things (IoT) based long range laser sensor perimeter surveillance system, the data from which is sent at regular intervals to a remote control station. The framework presents the design of an intrusion detection pole which houses the laser sensors and necessary electronics. To that extent, a generic embedded controller is designed to accommodate multiple single beam lasers of varying ranges, thus rendering the architecture, “range scalable”. In the proposed architecture, the laser sensors are geometrically arranged such that blind spots are avoided over the range of sensing. Lastly, the IoT enabled control room software architecture provides flexibility to visualize intrusion detection status and the system health from a remote location in an interactive graphical user interface. Field trials with the proposed IoT enabled surveillance system indicate very high detection accuracy for various scenarios of intrusion.

articleTitle: Impact of Author indexing from the Co-authorship Relation
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: As the the quality of research and spectrum of the publications are improving day by day, the citation parameter h-index [1] alone seems not sufficient to measure authors' performance. The citation is the relationship between two papers when one paper refers to another paper. In way to resolve the said issue, in this paper we have introduced a new author indexing parameter, <tex>$\mathbf{h}_{c}$</tex> -index based on the influence of the co-authors' h-index level. Our newly introduced index <tex>$(\mathbf{h}_{c})$</tex> looks through the co-authorship genealogy tree of an author and subsequently measures the related citation impacts created by every coauthors. This mechanism gives more accurate measurement for calculating author's citation index and the same we have observed in our experimental analysis, where we have seen substantial impact improvement while comparing actual h-index with <tex>$\mathbf{h}_{c}$</tex> -index for top 10 authors from Web of Universities<sup>1</sup><sup>1</sup>https://www.webometrics.info/enlhlargerthan100 ranking.

articleTitle: A Fog-Health Architecture for Early Alarming System of Heart Attack: A Deep Neural Network-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: In today's emerging world, technology is evolving day by day at its best. The healthcare sector is highly influenced by technological innovations. Fog computing is one of the modern technological innovations, which addresses various limitations associated with the cloud platform. This study aims to propose a fog-based healthcare architecture, as well as modules that show how Fog nodes work in this architecture. Related to this architecture, machine learning is used for real-time data analysis and future forecasts in the healthcare sector to ensure early diagnosis of heart patients. To that extent, the current study takes into account the deep neural network for classifying high-risk and low-risk patients. Thus, this research intends to implement the proposed model on the fog layer to ensure scalability and real-time data analytics. A heart disease dataset acquired from the UCI Machine Learning Datasets Repository (one of most important websites for collection of databases, domain theories, and data generators for machine learning community) is utilized for experimental purposes in this study. The results of the study show that the proposed DNN model has 82% accuracy in the classification of low-risk and high-risk patients. Moreover, it proves that the proposed model outperforms other state-of-the-art approaches, such as KNN, Decision Tree, and Random Forest by providing higher precision, recall, and F1-scores.

articleTitle: Optimized Decision Tree-based Early Phase Software Dependability Analysis in Uncertain Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Because of rapid development of software-based technology, early phase software dependability analysis has become very essential. The main purpose of this paper is to develop a novel classification model based on software dependability attributes for classification of software fault-prone modules during early phase of development. To carry out dependability analysis, early phase dependability attribute prediction is very essential. During early phase software metric value collection, metric values become uncertain due to difficulty of collection. Fuzzy Inference System (FIS) has been designed here to predict dependability attributes. A new algorithm for rule base generation has been proposed initially based on expert opinions for fuzzy inference system. These predicted software dependability attributes are applied to carry out dependability analysis. To classify software modules in early phase of development, an optimized Decision tree-based classification algorithm has been proposed to meet the main goal. Finally, Mahalanobis distance-based ranking technique has been developed based on different dependability attributes for ranking most non-dependable software modules. The proposed model has been validated based on software data sets. Software engineers will find the proposed model useful in allocating testing resources for most non-dependable software modules.

articleTitle: Application of S1 A1 Modes of Acoustic Emission Waves for Health Monitoring of Reinforced Concrete Slab
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Rigid Pavement which is principally a slab made of reinforced concrete is predominant in recent years for its long-lasting structural lifecycle. Comparable to the other RC structures, permanent deformation in the form of cracks are generated because of external loads. Such cracks are harmful from the serviceability point of the pavements. The literature available in this field suggests that acoustic emission (AE) is an efficient technique in the domain of structural health monitoring (SHM) to find the damage in real time. Additionally, the works done by the previous researchers show that investigation through the AE waveforms in the time-frequency domain using wavelet transform is also being used in the past for detecting the damage in concrete structures. However, as per the knowledge of the authors, the appropriateness of group velocity in detecting the damage, which has proved to be very effective in different types of materials, its application in RC slabs is rare as per the literature. In this study, the authors have attempted for damage detection in a sample RC slab with the use of the higher symmetric & anti-symmetric modes and group velocity of AE waves. The results found for localization are promising.

articleTitle: Impact of Meteorological Conditions on PM2.5 Concentration in Delhi
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Air pollution has been a widespread concern in recent years. It is an alarming issue due to the adverse effects of impurities, particularly on human health. The presence of the influence of the meteorological factors on the concentration of pollutants becomes the major subject of interest, as the determination of the correlation would help to explore the dynamics of the concentration of air pollutants. In this work, the existence of cross-correlation between pollutant PM2.5 and four meteorological factors, including temperature, humidity, pressure, and wind speed has been unraveled for Delhi using Multifractal cross-correlation detrended fluctuation analysis (MF-X-DFA) method. The daily data of the air pollutant PM2.5 and four meteorological factors have been obtained from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) for the years 2015 to 2019. The exploration shows that the cross-correlation between PM2.5 and all the four factors are persistent and long-range correlated also confirming multifractality. Meanwhile, the strength of the multifractal spectrum of wind speed is found to be strongest thus the effect of wind speed on PM2.5 concentration is obvious to be most pronounced. Hence it becomes evident from Hurst exponent values and multifractal spectrum that not only wind speed rather temperature, humidity, and wind speed combined can bring a massive change in concentration of PM2.5.

articleTitle: Secret Sharing Scheme: Based on LCD Code
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Data privacy is one of the main issues in communication technology and affects our daily lives. Secret sharing is essential in secure communication and has numerous applications in information security. Secret sharing is a methodology for accessing sensitive data by a few approved members. It shares the secret key in different structures among a few approved members, a specific number expected to recover the secret. There are many ways to deal with the development of secret sharing schemes. One of them depends on coding theory. There are many secret sharing schemes based on linear codes, but it is complicated to determine the access structure. We present a perfect scheme using linear complementary dual (LCD) codes to give more proficient and adaptable choices for secret sharing. We use the properties of LCD codes involving generator matrix in secret distribution and secret recovery phases. Likewise, we use a one-way hash function to verify the authorized participants by the dealer in the recovery phase. The performance analysis indicates that the proposed scheme is suitable for implementation in secret sharing.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Reduction of Induction Motor-based Electric Vehicle Using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Globally, the trend is toward reducing CO<inf>2</inf> emissions, and one way to do so is to switch from internal combustion to electric vehicles. To this aim, the electric drive system, which is the most critical component of an electric vehicle, has gained prominence and developed into a significant research issue. The induction motor is an excellent contender for electric vehicle applications because of its simplicity, robustness, and low maintenance. However, the conventional direct torque control scheme has a torque ripple issue, due to the use of hysteresis comparators and the availability of restricted voltage vectors. In this paper, the hysteresis comparator along with the switching table is replaced by an artificial neural network-based controller. The results indicate a significant reduction in torque ripple and improvement in dynamic performance.

articleTitle: Classification of Faults in UPFC Compensated Transmission Line using MDL selected Wavelet based DWT Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Protective relaying is used to recognize the abnormal signals that indicate faults in a power transmission system. As a result, in a transmission line, precise fault classification is an important issue. Therefore, wavelet technique is applied to classify the short circuit asymmetrical transmission line faults such as single line to ground and line to line faults for a transmission line with UPFC compensation in MATLAB/SIMULINK environment. To increase the efficacy of discrete wavelet transform (DWT) based fault classification scheme in UPFC compensated transmission line and to avoid the arbitrary selection of wavelet so that the complexity and time of handling large data set can be reduced, this paper proposes minimum description length (MDL) method for an optimal mother wavelet selection. Here, two orthogonal wavelet series such as Symlet and Daubechies wavelet are taken and MDL algorithm is utilized to select the suitable wavelet among twenty wavelets. To compare the performance of selected wavelet, max norm method is used to calculate the norm value. This similar experiment is also done for the faulty line without UPFC case. The MDL selected wavelet provides higher max norm value for faulty phase compared to the healthy one which shows the potency of the method.

articleTitle: A Dual-Frequency Microstrip Patch Antenna with Two Symmetrical Spur-lines for Wireless Communication Application
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: For dual-frequency operation, an inset-fed rectangular microstrip antenna (IRMA) loaded loaded with two symmetrical spur-lines along the two non-radiating edges of the rectangular shape is proposed. The proposed antenna has simulated resonance frequencies of 1.28 GHz and 1.89 GHz, allowing it to be used in wireless communication systems. The fundamental TM<inf>10</inf> mode and one activated lower order hybrid mode (<tex>$\mathbf{TM}_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}\mathbf{0}}$</tex> Mode-hybrid mode, where <tex>$\mathbf{0} < \boldsymbol{\alpha} < \mathbf{1}$</tex>) are the two exciting modes responsible for proposed antenna's dual-band operation. The proposed antenna has exhibited appropriate gain characteristics and stable radiation patterns for application in wireless communication domain.

articleTitle: Computational Study to Determine the Influence of Research on Enhancing API
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Faculty members at universities and institutes utilize the Academic Performance Indicator (API) of the University Grants Commission (UGC) to determine how to enhance their careers while remaining employed. Three main factors make up the API score: a) study actions connected to teaching, learning, and assessing; b) activities related to professional development, both within and outside the institute; and c) research and academic output. To determine each category's API score, we consider its unique collection of attributes and related data. In each faculty hierarchy, a faculty member's aggregate API score decides whether or not they advance from a lower level to a higher one. Researchers in this study analyzes the connections between API and the three types of data they find. Thirty samples were obtained from various sites to explore this through OLS regression analysis. Researchers observed a clear correlation between r values of 0.7338 and the first category. Further, r = 0.4231 suggests a moderate direct connection between the elements in category 2. The category three correlation value is 0.3756, indicating a weak direct link. The study found that faculty members in the education sector who seek to enhance their API scores must associate more with research-related activities.

articleTitle: Deployment of Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) for Reduction of Mutual Coupling and Cross-Polarization in MIMO Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a circular patch microstrip antenna integrated with FSS at 8.8GHz. The proposed antenna structure reduces mutual coupling (MC) between closely spaced microstrip antenna elements. This structure also reduces cross polarization (XP) radiation, which severely degrades the antenna performances. Here, we have taken two circular patches (centre-to-centre spacing is <tex>$\mathbf{0.028}\boldsymbol{\lambda} \mathbf{g},\boldsymbol{\lambda} \mathbf{g}=\mathbf{guided}$</tex> wavelength) and the FSS structure is inserted in between them in order to reduce the MC. In this work, the suppression of MC of 33dB and XP of 9dB are reported. This antenna structure is used as a multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) antenna in X-band.

articleTitle: Harvesting Renewable Energy Through Maglev Windmill
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: India being home to an extraordinary variety of climatic regions ranging from tropical in the south to temperate and alpine in the Himalayan in the North with an average wind speed of 15m/s. With raging population the electricity demand has been increasing steadily. Renewable energy sources are the now being incorporated along with the non-renewable energy sources to cope with the growing power supply. This paper proposes vertical axis wind turbine (VWAT) with a blend of Magnetic Levitation. Magnetic Levitation, or Maglev, is a method by which an object is suspended above another object with the help of magnetic field. Magnetic suspension in wind turbines is more advantageous than the conventional windmills as it eliminates friction due to any mechanical bearings. It thus makes it possible to harness wind energy even from low wind velocities with higher efficiency. This paper aims to achieve frictionless harnessing of the wind energy to give personal residential supplies.

articleTitle: An Energy-Efficient Clustering with Mobile Sink and Rendezvous Nodes for Data Collection in IoT-based Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: The inclusion of mobile sink(s) and rendezvous nodes has facilitated the data collection in Internet-of-Things-based wireless sensor networks to a great extent. In the sink-mobility-based clustered network enriched with rendezvous nodes, normal sensor nodes do not require to transmit their readings to the distant base station. Instead, they can transmit their data to the nearby mobile sink/rendezvous nodes saving their respective limited energy. Such a facility allows the saved energy to be utilized in further network operations, prolonging the overall network lifetime. However, clustering the nodes leading to energy-efficient operations in the aforementioned network scenario is still a challenging task. In this work, an existing scheme optimized-LEACH has been improved by formulating energy-aware clusters in the network. Various simulations establish the supremacy of the proposed scheme in terms of nodes' decay rate, average energy per node in the network, throughput, and nodes' distribution in the clusters. Experiments confirm that the proposed scheme achieves gains up to 167.56% in data packet delivery under varying network configurations.

articleTitle: Designing a Triple-Notched Bandpass Filter Using Ring and Split Ring Resonator for Ultra-wideband Communication Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: This paper proposes a triple-notched bandpass filter constructed by applying the combination of a ring structure-loaded multimode resonator (MMR) and split ring resonators (SRR) for ultra-wideband (UWB) communication devices. Filter passband spanning over a wide 7.71 GHz band (2.66 GHz-10.37 GHz) features three deep notches at 5.96 GHz, 6.53 GHz, and 8.82 GHz to shield the filter response from the interfering licensed wireless applications namely WLAN (5.9 GHz), super-extended C band <tex>$(\mathbf{5}.\mathbf{85}\ \mathbf{GHz}\sim \mathbf{7}.\mathbf{025}\ \mathbf{GHz})$</tex> used in satellite up conversion, X band <tex>$(\mathbf{8}\ \mathbf{GHz}\sim \mathbf{12}\ \mathbf{GHz})$</tex> radar used for ship traffic control and navigation respectively sharing the same transmission band as the proposed UWB bandpass filter. Besides other pertinent attributes of the filter such as low insertion loss <tex>$(\mathbf{0}.\mathbf{31}\sim \mathbf{1}.\mathbf{12})$</tex>, high fractional bandwidth (118.34%), broad upper stopband (5.05 GHz), and flat group delay <tex>$(\mathbf{0}.\mathbf{29}\sim \mathbf{0}.\mathbf{83}\ \mathbf{ns})$</tex> achieve a notable standard. These superior filter responses accompanying its compact size <tex>$(\mathbf{1}.\mathbf{15}\ \boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\mathbf{g}}\times \mathbf{0}.\mathbf{67}\ \boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\mathbf{g}})$</tex> establish the design to be acceptable for practical use.

articleTitle: Classification of Rice Varieties Using Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Consumers are concerned about the originality of rice varieties and quality, which causes rice varieties to be original. There are existing institutions that certify rice. Although different types of rice seeds visually appear similar in color, shape, and texture, it can be challenging to classify rice seed varieties with high precision. By analyzing images of objects, technology helps humans evaluate food grains. A system for identifying rice varieties was developed in this study. A rice image analysis and image processing were used to determine the rice. The classifier used is the convolutional neural network. The study collected and analyzed images of 22 different types of rice seeds planted in the Punjab region of India. The highest accuracy level our classification system can achieve is 77.5%. This result can be used in rice seed production plants in India to evaluate rice seed quality and identify varieties.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of BLDC Motor Control unit Using GaN-FET Inverter
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: In this paper, a comparative analysis on DC voltage to 3 phase AC voltage inverter using IGBT, Silicon Carbide (SiC) MOSFET and Gallium Nitride (GaN) MOSFET is presented. Characteristics like efficiency, switching frequency, torque and speed control of Brush less DC motor is presented. The simulation model of the BLDC motor is developed and is used to examine the performance of the power devices. Initially, a SiC-MOSFET controller is developed for the motors switching and speed control of the given BLDC motor. Further, the controller is upgraded to GaN-MOSFET and the performance of the BLDC motor is verified. Through extensive simulations using MATLAB. Performance parameters such as RMS current, voltage, duty cycle and efficiency are studied. Also, a reduction in area by 34% is achieved by replacing GaN MOSFET instead of SiC MOSFET.

articleTitle: Counterfeit Money Detection: A Hybrid Semi-Supervised GAN-based Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Despite recent advances in digital banking around the world, the use of banknotes is still predominant. In this context, the detection of fake money bills is important due to the severe impact of their circulation on the economic system. Automating and making detecting counterfeited bills accessible to anyone is still an under-investigated issue, which is mainly based on the visual inspection of bills. In this paper, we propose a novel semi-supervised generative adversarial network (GAN)-based detection approach that, by visually inspecting a bill, can determine if the latter is authentic or fake. Our method originally combines a parallelized GAN to a semi-supervised GAN. On a dataset of Tunisian bills, our method is able to achieve 100% accuracy, with a Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) below 1, i.e., generating diversified fake images with good quality. These performances are proven superior to those of several benchmark approaches.

articleTitle: Design of Optical Filter using Micro-Ring Resonator with Multiple Output Bus Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Modelling of vertically coupled five micro ring resonator (VCFMRR) is carried out in Z-domain as an optical add-drop filter (OADF). Design is done by delay line approach and transfer function of the system is evaluated by Mason's gain formula by representing the system according to signal flow graph theory. Then its characteristics are evaluated in MATLAB by determining free spectral range (FSR), crosstalk, Group Delay (GD) and Dispersion (DP). Wide FSR and negligible crosstalk with proper GD and DP characteristics prove its capability as a high speed optical add-drop filter in communication system. Its real-world performance is also evaluated in Opti-System software where exact open eye diagram proves its applicability in optical communication system. Performance evaluation by eye diagram is the uniqueness of VCFMRR model.

articleTitle: Fringing Field Capacitive Sensor: A Study of Different Configurations for Soil Moisture Measurement
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Soil moisture plays an important role in the healthy growth of plants and crops. With the advancement of technology, different sensors are being developed for monitoring soil moisture levels. In this research work, interdigitated (IDT) fringing field capacitive sensor of five different configurations viz. 1-1-1, 1-5-1, and square (type A, B, C) were designed and fabricated using printed circuit board (PCB) technology. The designed sensors were evaluated on two different types of soil. A simple capacitance to voltage (C-V) converter circuit using a 555 timer was used and the voltage to soil moisture calibration was done using the standard gravimetric method.

articleTitle: A new knowledge Measure on q-rung ortho pair fuzzy set and its application
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: While dealing with the ambiguity of human judgments, q-rung ortho pair fuzzy (q-ROPF) provide more freedom to the decision makers than fuzzy, intuitionistic fuzzy, and Pythagorean fuzzy. However, it is necessary to measure the degree of closeness between q-ROPF sets and crisp sets and also the difference between a crisp set and q-ROPF sets. In Literature, knowledge measure and entropy measures are used for this. In this paper, we introduce a new robust knowledge and entropy measures for q-ROPF sets and show that the proposed measures please the axiomatic properties of a knowledge and entropy measure. A Multi - Attribute Group Decision Making (MAGDM) framework based on COmplex Proportional Assessment (COPRAS) method is presented, by calculating the weights of the Decision Makers using knowledge measure under q-ROPF environment. The working and feasibility of the proposed MAGDM method are demonstrated, by applying it for the purchasing of the most preferred medical equipment for a hospital.

articleTitle: An Effort Towards Improving Automatic-Transcription Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: The automatic speech recognition (ASR) system is a modern popular emerging technological system with lots of scope for applications in different domains. However, developing a mature ASR system needs to address lots of challenges to accommodate the diversity of the accents of speakers from diverse countries, regions, communities, languages, dialects and many more. This work is an effort to understand the different aspects of improving modern automatic transcription systems. The performance on significant aspects like Accent detection, Gender Detection and Voice Recognition across five major audio features have been captured, analyzed and studied. Standard machine learning architecture has been applied to analyze the features and determine their impact on the performance of the transcription system. We observed a high level of accuracy on combined features and hope this study will help those who are working in ASR, and NLP.

articleTitle: Off-Axis Illumination of a Photomask Using Holographic Condenser Lens for Visible Light Lithoaraphy
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Photolithography has been indispensable part of modern VLSI industry. In photolithography desired fine feature of photo mask is projected on semiconductor chips using costly optical system. To achieve minimum feature size extreme ultraviolet lithography is used. However, cost of such system is very high and require high vacuum environment. The present high cost of extreme ultraviolet lithography has provoked the scientific community to search out alternative methods. Photolithography using visible light and properly designed holographic lenses to achieve desirable resolution at low cost is an attractive proposition for present VLSI industry. However, such holographic lenses are highly wavelength as well as angular selective. Wavelength selectivity means that if recorded holographic lenses are illuminated with radiation of different wavelength other than that of recording wavelength, their diffraction efficiency falls. Diffraction efficiency of such holographic lenses also falls rapidly with deviation in angle of reconstruction. Taking these facts into consideration, holographic lenses have been designed to give appreciable diffraction efficiency over desired wavelength range with large tolerance angle. All the analysis of this work has been performed using MATLAB software. Further such lenses may provide ease of off-axis illumination to improve imaging performance.

articleTitle: Design of Ultra Low Power 6T SRAM Cell Using 180 nm CMOS Technology for Access Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: The low power IC design has been a priority because of the recent growth in battery-operated portable devices. With the advancement in microcircuit technology, a low power, low transistor count and faster enhancement of static random-access memory (SRAM) has proved to be essential. Therefore, in such embedded systems, parallel read/write (R/W) access multiport SRAM bit-cells are the need of the hour. This area of SRAM design, along with CMOS technology, is being scaled up in different system-on-chip (SoC) products. In this paper, a 256-bit SRAM design is proposed using 180nm CMOS technology along with its peripheral circuits like 6 transistor (6T) cells, pre-charge circuit, write driver, column and row decoders, sense amplifiers, etc. in such a way that its operation speed is high compared to the other conventional SRAM cells. Our proposed SRAM has a speed of 12ns compared to other conventional SRAM's speed of about 400ns, which is way faster.

articleTitle: Predicting the COVID-19 Outbreak
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: This paper focuses on the use of mathematical modelling of propagation dynamics of infectious diseases. We use the discrete logistic model to propose a simple method to determine the start of coronavirus outbreak. Further, we apply the proposed method on real data of confirmed coronavirus cases from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Our results suggested that the proposed method can be used for raising an alarm of coronavirus outbreak.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Compact Rectangular Sectored UWB (Ultra-wideband) Antenna for Wireless Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: A compact rectangular sectored monopole ultra wide band (UWB) antenna is represented for WLAN and WiMAX applications. This article shows UWB characteristics with a wide operating bandwidth (1.5GHz - 9GHz) of 7.5GHz. It also shows the stop band filtering characteristics from 2.89GHz to 3.65GHz, which will be used to filter out the ISM band (2.4GHz), mobile communication (4.4GHz) and wireless data transfer (7.2GHz) signals. All the antenna characteristics parameter like gain, return loss, radiation pattern has been studied experimentally and verified it. From the simulated result it shows a good agreement.

articleTitle: Gene Essentiality Mediated Base Substitution in Escherichia coli genome: Machine Learning Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Several selection and mutation factors are known to influence evolution in the nucleotide sequence in the genome of organisms. Using the machine learning approach, we considered gene essentiality as a selection factor, and we investigated base substitution among essential and remaining gene sets in the Escherichia coli genome. RF and SVM classifiers achieved an AUC score of 75% each. The importance of the base substitution-based features differs in predicting essentiality. Features such as G to A substitutions, mutations within the amino group, and transversion mutations were found to be the most important features. In contrast, G to C, G to T, and T to C substitutions were among the least ones. This result indicates that the base substitution patterns in essential genes might differ from that in non-essential genes. The result of this manuscript will be helpful for understanding evolution at the molecular level.

articleTitle: Adjoint Based Optimization of NACA 4412 Airfoil
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: In this research paper, the shape optimization of the NACA 4412 airfoil has been carried out at 0<sup>0</sup> angle of attack and stall angle of attack, at moderate Reynolds number. The NACA 4412 airfoil has been used in sports planes which have a higher cruise speed compared to cargo planes. Hence, the shape of the airfoil needs to be optimized for achieving a higher lift to drag ratio. The adjoint method has been used to optimize the shape using ANSYS Fluent software.

articleTitle: A Digital Control Strategy for Wind Turbine-Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: This paper presents a digital control technique for the control of wind turbine-permanent magnet synchronous generator (WT-PMSG) in the MATLAB-Simulink environment. It is digital in the sense that instead of the commonly employed strategy of using complex transformations and design of various controllers, this technique uses only two embedded programs to achieve the desired control. The control strategy is simple yet very strong and gives results according to the theoretical concepts. The focus here is on the electrical side control of the WT-PMSG-inverter system under variable wind and variable load conditions, with the aim that it should be implementable in hardware without needing changes in the strategy. The simulation results in various operating modes validate the effectiveness of the proposed control technique. The achievement of this paper is the spike free pure sinusoidal load voltage without needing to design any conventional controller.

articleTitle: Novel 32nm CMOS Ternary Parity Generator-Checker
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Present study explores a new circuit topology for parity-based error detection in ternary domain. Proposed concept is discussed and applied to construct 4-trit Ternary even as well as odd parity generator-checker using conventional Enhancement-type Metal Oxide Semiconductor (MOS) transistor. Proposed idea adds two more redundant trit with the original ternary input sequence (i.e., one is for trit “1” and another is for trit “2”) to generate/check corresponding parity output. The complete circuit is designed on 32nm standard CMOS technology considering BSIM4 device model parameters with 1.0V supply rail at 27°C temperature. The ternary digits “0”, “1” and “2” are represented with 0V, 0.5V and 1.0V respectively. The extensive T-Spice transient simulations with all possible test patterns validate the proposed design. Ternary input for the simulation is applied using Piece-Wise-Linear (PWL) input source. Circuit speed-power response is evaluated and recorded.

articleTitle: IoT Based Bridge Automation with Hybrid Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: This paper emphasises on the prototype development and smooth running of IoT based tilted bridge with intelligent illumination and traffic management systems. The paper also focused on the mathematical analysis of power consumption of the bridge through hybridized power supply. The power supply of the total system is hybridized with MAGLEV windmill and Solar PV arrays. A provision to use any commercial power source for any emergency is also made available. The tilted bridge mechanism is based on an android application using Arduino UNO and HC05 Bluetooth module. In this present work, the performances of the fabricated tilted bridge with smart illumination and traffic system have been evaluated for different circumstances. The performance of the small system is found feasible for actual implementation.

articleTitle: A Study on Effect of Doping on Piezoelectric Materials
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: In the last few years, piezo ceramics and single crystals have been widely explored due to their significant electromechanical properties. A huge number of lead based and lead free piezo systems with doping effects were investigated during this period as supported from the various publications. The piezoelectric materials with perovskite structure exhibit the highest electromechanical coupling factor and piezoelectric coefficient due to existence of monotropic phase boundary (MPB) and tailor properties between soft and hard piezoelectric response. The piezoelectric material can be soft or hard depending upon the doping material, i.e., isovalent, acceptor and donor dopant. In general, electromechanical properties can be improved in lead-based piezoelectric materials by adding doping materials, where the dopant substitute either on A or B position of the ABO<inf>3</inf> perovskite structure. At this moment it is necessary to publish a review article to give the researcher a proper direction of future research for the further development of the piezosystem and selection of doping materials.

articleTitle: Ant Lion Based Optimized Leach Protocol to Enhance the Security and Transmission of Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: In wireless sensor networks (WSN), network delay is a prime issue for real-time applications. Most of the applications of WSN require the data in the minimum possible delay. But in extreme weather conditions, or harsh geographical terrains network delay is a common phenomenon. Therefore, a delay-tolerant network is required. Due to the ability to store and transport information within a brief period, Delay Tolerant Network (DTN) is a crucial means of communication, segment development, energy management, and extending the life of the network. Signal loss and packet loss during transfer are two ways that affect DTN communication. It results in higher energy consumption by certain nodes for retransmitting the same data again. It also makes the identification of cluster heads difficult as packets as well as signals are lost during transmission. Many strategies have been developed to address these concerns. As a result, a novel Ant Lion-based Optimized LEACH Algorithm (ALOLA) is created to improve DTN communication performance and to identify the nodes with low as well as high energy consumption rates, at an early stage of the energy-aware phase. Furthermore, a temporary route is also formulated to prevent sudden signal breakdown and packet drops. To generate and test results, the created method is applied in MATLAB with 100 nodes where Cluster Head (CH) is identified based on the threshold value. The created approach is compared to various current systems in terms of throughput, energy use, delay, delivery rate, and overhead using a series of scores.

articleTitle: Monitoring the Effects of Static Variable Orders on the Construction of BDDs
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: The increasing complexity of modern Integrated Circuits (ICs) results in more bug occurrences during their design. In this regard, formal verification techniques such as the methods based on Binary Decision Diagrams (BDDs) mathematically ensure the correctness of these ICs before fabrication. However, BDDs are very sensitive to input variable ordering. Most of the time, the construction of BDDs fails due to size explosion caused by unfavorable input variable ordering. A lot of research has been done in the past to find a good variable ordering method; however, the focus has always been on the endsize of BDDs which may not present the whole picture. In this paper, we present a framework to monitor the BDD size during construction. We argue that in addition to the endsize, the highest number of nodes, i.e. the peaksize, should also be taken into account when selecting the static variable ordering method. The proposed framework uses a variable order generator to compute an input variable order for a circuit and a BDD generator, with CUDD at its heart, to monitor important parameters in particular peaksize. With the help of the framework, we observe how popular static variable ordering heuristics affect the peaksize and endsize of BDDs using popular benchmark sets, i.e., ISCAS85, ISCAS89.

articleTitle: Opinion Mining and Sentiment Analysis on Twitter Data
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Sentiment analysis on Twitter data provides organizations with a quick and effective method to monitor the general public's sentiments about a brand, business, leaders, and so on. In recent years, a wide range of parameters and techniques for training sentiment analyzers for Twitter datasets has been researched, with various outcomes. To perform sentiment analysis on tweets, our proposed system extracts the posts from Twitter and analyzes tweet's sentiments towards products and services. In this paper, we used Long-Short Term Memory (a type of recurrent neural network) for Text Classification as it effectively enhances performance by memorizing vital information and detecting patterns. Using LSTM, we implemented an algorithm for automatic classification of text/tweets into six different sentiment classes, which can be extended further depending on the requirements. Our results showed a precision of 92.17% on testing the model based on test sequences and test labels and we visually expressed the sentiments in the form of a Pie-Chart.

articleTitle: State of Health and Life Cycle Prediction of In-Vehicle Lead Acid Battery
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Three-wheel battery-operated vehicles are the most popular kind of public transportation in Asian countries. The most apparent and cheaper version of on board energy generation source for this three wheeler is the traction battery pack mainly designed by lead acid batteries. In this study, an effort is made to close the gap by using a real-time battery monitoring system to investigate the battery health and battery aging-related parameter using modified Coulomb counting and a data-driven model. A proposed hardware based methodology is implemented to a series connected multiple lead-acid battery strings of a typical three-wheeler for the selected drive cycle. The method is used to measure the effective depth of discharge for an actual drive cycle, dynamically variation of internal resistance at different depth of discharge level, voltage and current to estimate and compare the battery health of a on board battery pack. The field test and comparison of the test results against three-wheelers provide evidence of the concept that internal resistance varies from 2% to 150% depending on battery ageing and significantly affects the terminal voltage drop at different discharge levels.

articleTitle: A Hand Gesture-Based Contact-less Interface for Electronic Health Records
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Clinical data monitoring and storing are essential components of continuous and preventive healthcare systems. Data such as blood pressure, pulse rate, temperature, etc., can be recorded by the hospital staff daily for in-patient subjects. The usual way of noting them down is to check different parameters using various medical instruments and write it on paper with the corresponding patient's details (e.g., name, patient-id, or government identity card number). However, after the outbreak of COVID-19, there is a set of World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines to behave in public places. Ordinary people and professionals feel hesitant to touch any media even if they have some protection such as gloves and sanitizer. In this crisis, there is a natural demand for contact-less activities instead of touch-based traditional ways. Gesture-based activities might be one of the low-cost alternatives to some sensor-based systems. This paper uses a profound learning-based finger point gesture to capture writing in the air and realize it on the screen through a predictive model. Here, the proposed framework has been demonstrated as a proof of concept to record blood pressure data for multiple patients without touching any electronic screen or paper. The proposed architecture is developed based on the gesture recognition and metric learning, which have been used to recognize different digits trained from the MNIST digit dataset. The mean test accuracy is reached 99.47% on the same dataset.

articleTitle: Random Forest Regression Model AugmenteD With KL Algorithm (RFRKL) To Minimize Power In FSM Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: The logic synthesis domain has recently benefited from improvements in intelligent learning, particularly for low power minimization. This research employed AI with the classic Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) to provide a low-power synthesis. Initially, from an input State Transition Graph (STG), a Markov process probabilistic model is formed and the next KL algorithm is applied using the partitioning method where it calculates the Weighted Hamming Distance (WHD). To find the minimum power with respect to proper state encoding using SIS tool is a NP-Hard problem and rather time consuming. When the database has been generated, a Random-Forest regression model is trained to replace the SIS tool in order to predict the power for multi-level realizations based on the database. The model is even more effective at making predictions, with a maximum test error of 4.584% and an average test error of 0.799 %. According to the results, the augmented-based framework accelerates the process on average 1.5 times faster than the traditional simulation-based framework.

articleTitle: Effect of Heat-Treatment on Electrical Properties of Ag2S Doped Chalcogenide Glassy System
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: XRD analysis validated the size of nanocrystallites in the current chalcogenides, Ag<inf>2</inf>CdI<inf>4</inf>, Cd<inf>10</inf>S<inf>5.71</inf>Se<inf>4.29</inf>, CdS<inf>0.75</inf>Se<inf>0.25</inf>, S<inf>27.64</inf>Se<inf>4.36</inf>, Ag2Se, S8, and I<inf>2</inf>. Changes in heat-treatment time show that dislocations are increasing and crystallite diameters are shrinking. The bulk and grain boundary areas of the current system are represented by complex impedance graphs. The disordered energy is discovered to be lower than the DC activation energy, and the net change in DC activation energies <tex>$(\mathbf{\Delta} \mathbf{E}_{\boldsymbol{\sigma}})$</tex> is playing a pivotal role to explore the phenomena of the optical and multi-phonon process of charge carrier hopping from one localized state to the next. The insertion of additional electron/polaron, as well as feeble Ag<sup>+</sup> ions due to Cd-Ag exchange, is expected to enhance DC conductivity. However, the presence of chalcogens in the current system is likely to result in poor polaron conduction. The overall AC conduction behavior appears to change back and forth between the normal and heat-treated samples under investigation. The bipolar hopping process can be used to predict this major conduction mechanism for AC conductivity. Because of its stabilized DC conductivity, the current system could be a useful electrolyte for batteries.

Author Keywords: complex impedance plots and grain boundary regions

articleTitle: Risk and Weightage Based Route Prediction System Using Machine Learning: A Review
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: Transportation is the key context ingredient in modern life. Optimised route prediction is the vital aspect for commercial enterprises and individuals also. Proper route prediction not only helps to save time, fuel, and money, it additionally prevents accident, air pollution. Operational efficiency like uncertain event and incident can be cause for delay delivery, reaching late in destination that cause also the revenue loss for organisation and individual also. According to the 2019 Urban Mobility Report in 2017, congestion caused urban Americans to travel an extra 8.8 billion hours and purchase an extra 3.3 billion gallons of fuel for a congestion cost of $166 billion. Trucks account for $21 billion (12 percent) of the cost, much more than their 7 percent of traffic. The average auto commuter spends 54 hours in congestion and wastes 21 gallons of fuel due to congestion at a cost of $1,010 in wasted time and fuel. [1]. Nowadays drivers are using different Map software and GPS(Global Positioning System) to choose the appropriate route but sudden changes like climate variation, road congestion due to social gathering, road construction work etc. are difficult to incorporate in existing map software. With the development of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and Internet of Things (IoT), transportation data has become more and more ubiquitous. This triggers a series of data-driven research to investigate transportation phenomena. Among them, Machine learning theory is considered one of the most promising techniques to tackle tremendous high-dimensional data. Machine Learning models are able to predict more accurate rote in transportation systems. This paper deeply analyses existing route prediction systems and different technology used in those systems. The Authors will focus on improving this route prediction using a machine learning model.

articleTitle: Fusion-Based Segmentation and Classification of Novel Coronavirus or Pneumonia from Chest X-ray Images Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2022 International Interdisciplinary Conference on Mathematics, Engineering and Science (MESIICON)
abstract: The deadfall widespread of coronavirus (SARS-Co V-2) disease has trembled every part of the earth and has significant disruption to health support systems in different countries. In spite of such existing difficulties and disagreements for testing the coronavirus disease, an advanced and low-cost technique is required to classify the disease. For the sense of reason, supervised machine learning (ML) along with image processing has turned out as a strong technique to detect coronavirus from human chest X-rays. In this work, the different methodologies to identify coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) are discussed. It is essential to expand a fully automatic detection system to restrict the carrying of the virus load through contact. Various deep learning structures are present to detect the SARS-CoV-2 virus such as ResNet50, Inception-ResNet-v2, AlexNet, Vgg19, etc. A dataset of 10,040 samples has been used in which the count of SARS-CoV-2, pneumonia and normal images are 2143, 3674, and 4223 respectively. The model designed by fusion of neural network and HOG transform had an accuracy of 98.81% and a sensitivity of 98.65%.
